full_judgment: 2. Facts in short are that the respondent No. 2 while employed in the establishment of the petitioner went on sick leave for two days with effect from 25,7.78 but on the expiry of his leave he did not report for duty. The respondent No. 2, however, sent a telegram to the petitioner on 31.7.78 for extension of his leave without mentioning the period of extension. No application was also filed at that time or soon thereafter for leave. The management however sent a telegram to the Respondent on 17.8.78 to appear before the Medical Board. The respondent No. 2 in reply sent a Medical Certificate and prayed for extension of one month leave as advised by his physician as shown in a Medical Certificate, Ext. D, dated 27.8.78. The Management did not accept the certificate since it contained interpolation and over writing. Thereafter the charge-sheet dated 19.978 was issued to the respondent No. 2 for alleged misconduct u/s. 17 (3) (d) of the Employment of Labour (Standing Order) Act, 1965 in remaining absent without leave since 27.7.78. The respondent submitted an explanation which was found to be unsatisfactory and it led to an enquiry. The enquiry committee found the petitioner guilty of the charge, and the management accepting the finding of the enquiry committee dismissed had been challenged before the Labour Court. The petitioner opposed the application contending inter alia that the respondent No. 2 com-mitted misconduct in remaining absent for more than ten days after expiry of the leave without leave or permission and that the enquiry committee after making a proper enquiry found the respondent No. 2 guilty and the management accepting the recommendation of the enquiry committee rightly dismissed the respondent.
